questions.text: Is your PIMS scope defined — covering systems, products, regions and teams that handle personal information, with clear in/out boundaries?
Is privacy ownership assigned — a named privacy lead or DPO with documented responsibilities, escalation paths and decision authority?
Is a Record of Processing Activities (ROPA) maintained — covering purpose, data types, systems, vendors, lawful basis and retention?
Is a DPIA (privacy risk assessment) methodology defined and applied before high-impact changes, new processing or vendor onboarding?
Are privacy-by-design controls implemented — data minimisation, defined retention periods, role-based access and automated deletion?
Are individual rights requests (access, erasure, correction, portability) handled through a defined workflow within a committed timeframe?
Is privacy training role-based, assigned to all relevant staff, with completion tracked and available for audit?
Are third-party processors assessed before onboarding, with privacy obligations (DPAs) in contracts and ongoing reviews documented?
Are cross-border data transfers identified, assessed for risk, documented, and covered by safeguards where required?
Are management reviews held at planned intervals, covering PIMS performance, risks, incidents, KPIs and improvement decisions?
